headline: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: SOUTH-WEST MONSOON FORECAST
fullText:
Ministry of Earth Sciences

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: SOUTH-WEST MONSOON FORECAST

12 AUG 2026 12:39PM by PIB Delhi

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued its First Stage Long Range Forecast for the 2026 Southwest Monsoon Season on 13th April 2026, predicting below-normal seasonal rainfall at 92% of the Long Period Average (LPA). This was updated in the Second Stage forecast to 90% of the LPA, while anticipating the development of El Niño conditions. In line with these predictions, June recorded 35% below-normal rainfall with 70% of districts experiencing deficits. Although July recorded 1% above the LPA on an all-India scale due to strong rainfall in Central India, significant spatial disparities remained, with 47% of districts facing deficient or large-deficient rainfall. As of 2nd August 2026, cumulative seasonal rainfall stands at 12% below the LPA, which remains broadly consistent with IMD's initial seasonal forecast despite expected intra-seasonal variations.

As predicted, weak El Niño conditions formed over the equatorial Pacific in June 2026 and intensified to moderate strength, acting as a major large-scale climate driver in suppressing monsoon circulation across the country. This phenomenon directly contributed to the overall 12% cumulative deficit and widespread regional rain deficits affecting 47 % districts as of early August. The primary implications of these El Niño conditions include prolonged dry spells, localized meteorological drought, lower soil moisture, and moisture stress on rain-fed crops and water reservoir levels. IMD is continuously monitoring these climate drivers and issuing updated advisories to assist relevant Ministries and State Governments in disaster preparedness and agricultural planning.

Cumulative rainfall up to 5th August 2026 revealed substantial spatial deviations across meteorological subdivisions. Significant rainfall deficiencies (ranging between 20% and 38% below normal) were recorded across sixteen subdivisions, including Bihar (-38%), Arunachal Pradesh (-36%), Assam & Meghalaya (-35%), Coastal A.P. & Yanam (-35%), Lakshadweep (-33%), Punjab (-33%), Rayalaseema (-32%), East Uttar Pradesh (-30%), Jharkhand (-30%), Haryana, Chandigarh & Delhi (-26%), Kerala & Mahe (-22%), East Madhya Pradesh (-22%), East Rajasthan (-22%), Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram & Tripura (NMMT) (-21%), Coastal Karnataka (-21%), and South Interior Karnataka (-20%), among others. Deficient regions face potential crop stress and reduced water storage. IMD continues to provide sub-divisional alerts to guide proactive risk management by Central and State agencies.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

headline: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi releases Autobiography of Former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi releases Autobiography of Former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind

Today, we have the opportunity to release the autobiography of Shri Ram Nath Kovind ji; I am happy to be a part of this program: PM

His journey reflects a life dedicated to public service and the progress of our nation:PM

My prolonged acquaintance with Kovind Ji and his special affection and warmth towards me have been my greatest assets: PM

Mahatma Gandhi, Babasaheb Ambedkar, Jyotiba Phule, and Savitribai Phule dreamed of forging a new India, where the absolute poorest and the most disadvantaged could get the chance to reach the very top: PM

Individuals like Kovind Ji have not merely transformed their own lives through their diligence and competence, they have also played a pivotal role in bringing that centuries-old dream and vision to fruition: PM

Even after retiring as President; he is working on 'One Nation, One Election'; Its resolution can start a new chapter in Democracy: PM

12 AUG 2026 12:39PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today released the autobiography of former President of India, Shri Ram Nath Kovind, titled “Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles”, at Vigyan Bhavan, New Delhi. Addressing the gathering, the Prime Minister said “Today we have got the opportunity to release the autobiography of Shri Ram Nath Kovind ji, and I am happy that I have become a part of this program,” remarked Shri Modi.

Reflecting on his deep personal connection with the former President, the Prime Minister highlighted his profound respect for Kovind ji's guidance and affection over the years. “My prolonged acquaintance with Kovind Ji, the good fortune of knowing him closely, his guidance in his capacity as President, and, above all, his special affection and warmth towards me, these have been my greatest assets,” noted Shri Modi.

Praising the depth of the former President's character and capabilities, the Prime Minister asserted that the literary work will serve as an enduring testament to the nation's democratic values. “I can say with full confidence that the autobiography of Ram Nath Kovind ji will in itself become a heritage for the Indian democracy and Indian society,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Acknowledging the vastness of Kovind ji's lifelong contributions to the nation, the Prime Minister, refraining from providing excessive details, encouraged the audience to discover the narrative firsthand. “In a book release, there should only be a 'curtain raiser', and it is better only if you all get the full benefit of the book by reading it!” remarked Shri Modi.

Highlighting the educational value of the memoir for the younger demographic, the Prime Minister expressed his desire for future generations to draw inspiration from the former President's words. “The new generation of the country should also read his writing and his experiences, from which everyone will get to learn a lot,” asserted Shri Modi.

Analyzing the title of the book, “Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles”, the Prime Minister interpreted its dual significance regarding personal hardship and national democratic success. “The struggles of life are his personal, but the victory achieved as a result of those struggles belongs to the Republic of India and its democracy,” observed Shri Modi.

Contrasting common human tendencies with the former President's magnanimity, the Prime Minister pointed out that while many blame society for their hardships, Kovind ji's generous heart deeply rooted in Indian values views society as an equal partner in his success. “When the heart is generous and there are Indian values, a person does not waste time finding faults in society, but focuses on its positive side,” noted Shri Modi.

Recounting a deeply tragic childhood incident from the autobiography, the Prime Minister shared the heartbreaking story of Kovind ji's mother losing her life in a house fire while trying to save essential household items in Kanpur Dehat. “You can imagine such an accident at a young age and losing a mother like this, how painful this must have been!” remarked Shri Modi.

Highlighting the resilience forged through this tragedy, the Prime Minister explained how a neighboring mother stepped in to assist with Kovind ji's upbringing, an act that profoundly shaped his understanding of societal harmony. “From this, he understood the power of unity and harmony of society, and those difficulties made Kovind ji even stronger,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Emphasizing the crucial paternal role following the tragedy, the Prime Minister noted how Kovind ji's father admirably steered the family and instilled strong values in his children. “The way he handled his family and gave values to the children is why Kovind ji considers his father his hero,” observed Shri Modi.

Tracing Kovind ji's reliance on education to overcome his lack of resources, the Prime Minister highlighted his extraordinary ascent to the highest office in the land. “He worked hard and did not let the lack of resources become a weakness, reaching a position which people had not even imagined then,” asserted Shri Modi.

Praising the former President's enduring humility, the Prime Minister recalled a deeply emotional public moment when Kovind ji returned to his village of Paraunkh, bowing to the soil and touching the feet of his former teachers. “His conduct placed such a picture of India's values in front of the world on which every Indian can feel proud,” noted Shri Modi.

Reflecting on the historical socio-economic setbacks caused by centuries of slavery, the Prime Minister honored the relentless struggles and visionary dreams of historical figures like Mahatma Gandhi, Baba Saheb Ambedkar, and Jyotiba Phule. “How many such great personalities had dreamed of the reconstruction of an India where the poorest of the poor could get the opportunity to reach the top,” remarked Shri Modi.

Connecting these historical aspirations to modern achievements, the Prime Minister credited figures like Kovind ji for actively realizing the centuries-old vision of an egalitarian society through sheer hard work. “Personalities like Kovind ji with their hard work and ability did not just change their own life, they also played a role in realizing that dream of centuries,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Stressing the continuous need for dedicated youth to carry this mission forward, the Prime Minister called for a generation that remains undeterred by obstacles and maintains the courage to forge paths toward national self-reliance. “With this very change, the resolution of building an empowered India will be fulfilled, and the path to a self-reliant and Viksit Bharat will be paved,” asserted Shri Modi.

Positioning the autobiography as a crucial motivational tool, the Prime Minister suggested that the detailed account of Kovind ji's life will serve as a definitive guide for shaping this necessary youth power. “The inspiration needed for the creation of such youth power, this autobiography of Kovind ji can become an important source of that,” observed Shri Modi.

Detailing Kovind ji's political genesis, the Prime Minister noted how working alongside Morarji Desai channeled his inherent desire for national service into a dedicated career in politics. “The feeling of national service that was inside Kovind ji, he found a path for it by working with Morarji,” remarked Shri Modi.

Highlighting a consistent track record of service, the Prime Minister commended Kovind ji's unwavering dedication to duty across his various roles in Parliament, as Governor, and eventually as President. “He worked making service his goal, and his tenure in Parliament is a witness to this,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Pointing to Kovind ji's tireless post-presidential contributions, the Prime Minister praised his ongoing leadership on critical national issues like 'One Nation, One Election', which holds the potential to revolutionize the country's democratic framework. “I believe the people of the country can learn a lot from this dedication to duty and spirit of service of Kovind ji,” asserted Shri Modi.

Acknowledging the immense difficulty of authoring an autobiography while remaining highly active in public life, the Prime Minister expressed gratitude to Kovind ji for completing this vital societal contribution. “Kovind ji has done this work for all of us because there is so much in his life in which all the people coming from poor deprived sections can see the shadow of their own life,” noted Shri Modi.

Detailing the broader moral lessons encapsulated within the text, the Prime Minister emphasized how the former President's narrative illustrates the enduring power of maintaining purity and honesty during the toughest times. “Kovind ji has continuously given this inspiration to the society on how this purity gives us the strength for national service while fulfilling the responsibilities of different posts,” observed Shri Modi.

Concluding the address with a strong endorsement of the book's historical value, the Prime Minister expressed absolute certainty that the literary work will serve as an essential archive for both personal and national milestones. “I am confident Kovind ji's autobiography will safely preserve not only the important memories of his life but also of our democracy,” affirmed Shri Modi.

12 AUG 2026 12:39PM by PIB Delhi

The National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), is entrusted with developing technologies for the reliable and sustainable harvesting of polymetallic nodules from the deep ocean. A seabed mining system has been developed, for which mobility and system-powering trials were successfully undertaken at a depth of 5270 m at the Central Indian Ocean Basin (CIOB) site allocated by the International Seabed Authority (ISA). Ministry of Earth Sciences has signed contracts with the International Seabed Authority (ISA) for exploration of seabed minerals, namely Polymetallic Nodules (PMN) and Polymetallic Sulphides (PMS) in the Indian Ocean in the areas beyond National jurisdiction. The Resource Assessment and the Environmental Impact Assessment studies are carried out as per the contractual obligations and guidelines set out by the ISA. Multidisciplinary Oceanographic Studies are conducted in the Indian contract areas under the exploration contract to establish baseline environmental conditions and assess the possible effects of exploration activities on deep sea ecosystems. Presently, only the activities related to exploration of deep seabed minerals in the international seabed are permitted.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

12 AUG 2026 12:38PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India, through the Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology (CMLRE), Kochi, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, implements a comprehensive programme to assess and monitor Marine Living Resources (MLR) in India’s Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), aligned with the institutions' mandate.

In the last three years (2023–2026), CMLRE has undertaken ~19 surveys for the assessment of fishery resources and marine biodiversity in the Indian EEZ.

Scientific data generated through CMLRE is being utilised to support sustainable MLR management, marine conservation, and evidence‑based policy formulation. Key applications include the estimation of the potential fishery yield of the Indian EEZ (conducted every eight years), identification of ESBAs (Ecologically & Biologically Significant Areas), development of biodiversity inventories and genomic reference libraries, identification of fish spawning grounds and seasons, submission of data for national and international commitments (including the Convention on Biological Diversity and SDG-14), and publication of scientific reports on deep sea and distant‑water fishery resources of the Indian EEZ.

The steps/initiatives to strengthen scientific research, ecosystem monitoring, and long‑term assessment of marine living resources in Indian waters are elaborated below.

Long‑term observations and marine ecosystem monitoring, also as part of the MLR Programme, covering fishery resources, biodiversity, and environmental drivers across the Indian EEZ, and their assessment and mapping.

Bhavasagara National Repository for long‑term preservation and documentation of deep‑sea biological specimens.

Advanced scientific technologies and genomic reference libraries, including digitisation of collections and data to support modern taxonomic and biodiversity research.

Capacity building and collaboration with national and international institutions in marine sciences.

Scientific studies for supporting conservation of vulnerable marine ecosystems and the sustainable management of marine living resources aligned to national priorities and international commitments.

headline: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Status of Early Warning Systems
fullText:
Ministry of Earth Sciences

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Status of Early Warning Systems

12 AUG 2026 12:37PM by PIB Delhi

Under Mission Mausam, the India Meteorological Department has strengthened its observational network with 50 Doppler Weather Radars, 1,008 Automatic Weather Stations, and 6,885 rain gauge stations nationwide. These advancements have improved severe weather forecast accuracy by 40–50% over the past decade, significantly reducing cyclone track, landfall, and intensity errors. For flood monitoring, 25 Flood Meteorological Offices issue daily 7-day Quantitative Precipitation Forecasts across 220 sub-basins to assist the Central Water Commission, alongside operational integrated flood warning systems in Chennai and Mumbai.

Additionally, INCOIS acts as the designated Tsunami Service Provider for 28 Indian Ocean Rim nations, using real-time ocean observations and multi-channel dissemination platforms like Sachet and the SAMUDRA app to issue alerts. Through the UNESCO-IOC Tsunami Ready Recognition Programme, 26 coastal villages in Odisha have already been recognized for local preparedness.

The Multi-Hazard Early Warning- Decision Support System (MHEW-DSS) is an advanced digital forecasting platform developed by the India Meteorological Department (IMD), under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), using open-source technology and in-house expertise. Introduced as a landmark digital transformation initiative under Mission Mausam, the system strengthens India's real-time weather monitoring and early warning capabilities. The MHEW-DSS reflects the Government of India's vision of a "Weather Ready and Climate Smart Nation" and embodies the philosophy of "Har Har Mausam, Har Ghar Mausam," ensuring that timely and actionable weather information reaches every household, sector, and region.

Climate research in the Himalayan region focuses on cascading hazards, glaciology, and hydrological dynamics. NCESS leads flood and hydrological modelling for Garhwal Himalaya hazard studies, while NCPOR conducts long-term monitoring of eight benchmark glaciers across Himachal Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh from its high-altitude 'Himansh' research station at 4,080 meters. In coastal zones, INCOIS research under the Deep Ocean Mission projects mean sea-level rise along the Indian coastline between 0.62 meters and 0.87 meters by 2100 under a high-emission scenario. Meanwhile, NIOT maintains an extensive ocean observational network consisting of OMNI moored buoys, coastal HF radars, and tsunami buoys. These field efforts are complemented by MoES policy publications and IMD’s GIS-based web Climate Hazards and Vulnerability Atlas of India.

The Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune, under its ongoing project “Metropolitan Air Quality and Weather Forecasting Services (MAQWFS)”, is conducting an integrated atmospheric and cryospheric observational experiment over the Gangotri–Gaumukh and Satopanth Glaciers. As part of the Glacier Expedition, IITM under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) has undertaken mobile atmospheric observations along the Gangotri–Gaumukh–Tapovan transect and established a continuous monitoring station at Bhojbasa, located at approximately 3,500 metres above mean sea level. These observations are aimed at improving the understanding of atmospheric processes and their interactions with the cryosphere in the Himalayan region.

The National Center for Seismology under the Ministry of Earth Sciences has significantly expanded the National Seismological Network from 86 observatories in 2014 to 174 active observatories across the country. To prioritize high-hazard areas, 89 of these observatories are strategically placed within high-risk Seismic Zones IV and V. This continuous real-time monitoring capability has successfully lowered the nationwide earthquake detection threshold to Magnitude 3.0, with an enhanced threshold of Magnitude 2.5 achieved for Delhi-NCR and the North-Eastern regions.

For the current financial year 2026–27, the proposed budget allocation for the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research under the Polar Science and Cryosphere Research (PACER) scheme stands at ₹270.00 crore.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

headline: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: FLOOD FORECASTING AND EARLY WARNING SYSTEM IN NORTHEAST INDIA
fullText:
Ministry of Earth Sciences

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: FLOOD FORECASTING AND EARLY WARNING SYSTEM IN NORTHEAST INDIA

12 AUG 2026 12:36PM by PIB Delhi

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued advance district-level rainfall forecasts and colour-coded impact-based warnings for all districts of Upper Assam, including Jorhat, Golaghat, Sivasagar, and Charaideo, prior to and during the heavy to very heavy rainfall activity from 18th to 20th July 2026. The forecasts issued by IMD for the State captured the occurrence of the heavy and very heavy rainfall events with a lead time of 7 days, accompanied by daily colour-coded warnings valid for the subsequent 7 days. Standard rainfall classifications per IMD guidelines were followed, categorizing rainfall intensity levels across light, moderate, heavy, and very heavy precipitation alongside spatial distribution scales ranging from scattered to widespread coverage.

The high rainfall event was driven by key synoptic weather systems and atmospheric components during 17th to 20th July 2026. On 17th July 2026, the mean sea level monsoon trough extended towards the Northeast Bay of Bengal, accompanied by a low-pressure area over Gangetic West Bengal and adjoining regions, along with an upper air cyclonic circulation over Northeast Assam and its neighborhood extending up to 1.5 km above mean sea level. Between 18th and 20th July 2026, the upper air cyclonic circulation over Northeast Assam shifted towards Central Assam and adjoining Nagaland between 1.5 km and 3.1 km above mean sea level and persisted through 20th July. Additionally, an upper air cyclonic circulation over North Jharkhand and adjoining Bihar, along with a connected atmospheric trough extending across Gangetic West Bengal and Bangladesh to Tripura, further sustained the strong monsoonal activity across Upper Assam. Daily weather bulletins detailing the episode remain archived and available with the Regional Meteorological Centre, Guwahati.

IMD regularly assesses the performance, accuracy, and lead time of its extreme heavy rainfall forecasts and warnings across all regions of Assam, divided into sub-regions including West Assam, South Assam, Central Assam, and Northeast Assam. The evaluation parameters primarily measure overall accuracy, detection probability, threat handling, and false alarm frequencies for lead times spanning from Day 1 to Day 5. In West Assam, the overall forecast accuracy expressed as Percentage of Correct forecasts (PC) ranges from 72.14% on Day 1 to 80.94% on Day 5. The Probability of Detection (POD) stands at 0.6345 for Day 1 and gradually decreases to 0.1209 on Day 5. Correspondingly, the False Alarm Ratio (FAR) ranges from 0.738 on Day 1 to 0.9613 on Day 5, while the Critical Success Index (CSI) moves between 0.1936 on Day 1 and 0.0264 on Day 5.

In South Assam, the Percentage of Correct forecasts remains consistently high, ranging from 60.48% on Day 1 up to 84.68% on Day 5. The Probability of Detection records a value of 0.525 for Day 1 and decreases to 0.0425 for Day 5. The False Alarm Ratio varies from 0.855 on Day 1 to 0.75 on Day 5, whereas the Critical Success Index records values ranging between 0.12 on Day 1 and 0.0425 on Day 5. In Central Assam, the forecasting system demonstrates high overall accuracy, with the Percentage of Correct forecasts improving from 66.36% on Day 1 to 80.18% on Day 5. The Probability of Detection starts at 0.6929 on Day 1 and shifts to 0.0757 by Day 5. The False Alarm Ratio ranges from 0.8114 on Day 1 to 0.8883 on Day 5, while the Critical Success Index records a performance ranging between 0.1671 on Day 1 and 0.0429 on Day 5.

In Northeast Assam, the Probability of Detection is notable at 0.7229 on Day 1 and 0.1857 on Day 5, supported by a lower False Alarm Ratio ranging between 0.3913 on Day 1 and 0.5538 on Day 5. The Critical Success Index shows strong performance ranging from 0.4275 on Day 1 to 0.19 on Day 5. The overall forecast accuracy in terms of Percentage of Correct forecasts for Northeast Assam remains stable across the lead times, measuring 58.47% on Day 1 and 51.61% on Day 5.

India Meteorological Department considers large-scale climate drivers, including the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), while preparing seasonal rainfall forecasts over India, including Northeast India. IMD's seasonal forecasting system utilizes a combination of dynamical coupled climate models and statistical techniques that incorporate various oceanic and atmospheric parameters such as sea surface temperatures, atmospheric circulation, ENSO, IOD, and other climate indicators. These factors are assessed collectively to generate probabilistic forecasts of seasonal rainfall.

For Northeast India, ENSO and IOD influence rainfall variability. While El Niño is generally associated with below-normal southwest monsoon rainfall over most parts of India, Northeast India receives normal to above-normal rainfall during some El Niño years. The relationship between El Niño and rainfall over Northeast India is relatively weak and complex compared to the rest of the country, as rainfall over the region is strongly influenced by factors such as Bay of Bengal moisture transport, monsoon circulation, and orographic effects. Consequently, the impact of El Niño on Northeast India's seasonal rainfall is not uniform and varies from one event to another. Currently, moderate El Niño conditions are prevailing, while IOD remains neutral, and these conditions have been incorporated into IMD's seasonal rainfall outlooks. However, flood risk over Northeast India also depends on short-duration extreme rainfall events, river basin conditions, and catchment characteristics; therefore, flood-risk assessments are based on both seasonal climate outlooks and operational weather forecasts.

With regard to flood-risk assessment, IMD's rainfall forecasts and weather warnings form important meteorological inputs for flood forecasting. Operational flood forecasting in the country is carried out by the Central Water Commission (CWC), which integrates IMD's weather forecasts with hydrological observations, river gauge data, and hydrological models for issuing flood forecasts and warnings. Thus, ENSO and IOD contribute to seasonal assessment of rainfall variability and flood potential, while actual flood forecasts are based primarily on observed and forecast rainfall, river conditions, and hydrological modelling.

To improve spatial resolution and accuracy at the sub-district level in the Northeast India, the advanced Numerical Weather Prediction model development has been operationalized, featuring the high-resolution New Bharat Forecasting System (BharatFS) at 6 km to cater to block and panchayat levels, supported by the enhanced computing power of the "Arunika" and "Arka" systems. Under Mission Mausam, the advanced Multi-Hazard Early Warning-Decision Support System (MHEW-DSS) has been introduced for real-time monitoring and forecasting. Furthermore, the observational network over Northeast India is being enhanced through the installation of state-of-the-art observing systems.

This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

- **FAME India Scheme Phase-II (01.04.2019–31.03.2024):** Total budgetary support of ₹11,500 crore; supported sale of ~16.72 lakh EVs (e-2Ws, e-3Ws, e-4Ws); deployed 5,299 e-buses as on 31.07.2026; allocated ₹912.50 crore for EV public charging stations (EVPCS), with 9,583 EVPCS installed.
- **PLI Scheme for Automobile & Auto Components (notified 23.09.2021):** Budgetary outlay of ₹25,938 crore for Advanced Automotive Technology products including EVs.
- **PLI Scheme for ACC Battery Storage (notified 09.06.2021):** Budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore; targets 50 GWh domestic ACC manufacturing capacity; 40 GWh awarded to four beneficiary firms (end-use agnostic).
- **PM EDRIVE Scheme (notified 29.09.2024):** Outlay of ₹10,900 crore; supports incentivization of ~28.30 lakh EVs (e-2W, e-3W, e-Trucks, e-buses, e-Ambulances); ₹4,391 crore allocated for 14,028 e-buses (14,000 allocated); ₹2,000 crore for pan-India EVPCS deployment.
- **PM e-Bus Sewa–Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme (notified 28.10.2024):** Outlay of ₹3,435.33 crore; aims to support >38,000 e-buses; covers 27,555 e-buses as on 10.07.2026 (10,000 under MoHUA, 14,000 under PM EDRIVE, 3,555 under State/STU initiatives).
- **Phased Manufacturing Programme (PMP):** Mandates domestic manufacturing of EV components, including battery packs, in a phased manner.
- **Supportive Policy Measures:** GST on EVs and chargers reduced to 5%; battery-operated vehicles granted green license plates and permit exemption; advisory issued to states to waive road tax on EVs.
- **Cumulative EVs Supported under MHI Schemes (as on 30.06.2026):** FAME-I: 2.80 lakh; FAME-II: 16.72 lakh; PM EDRIVE: 26.59 lakh; PLI Auto & Auto Components: ~21.30 lakh (up to 31.03.2026).
- **Charging Infrastructure (as on 07.08.2026):** 67,657 EV chargers installed across States/UTs, including 1,139 battery swapping station chargers.

fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

World Elephant Day

Celebrating Elephants, Ecosystems and Coexistence

12 AUG 2026 11:27AM by PIB Delhi

World Elephant Day highlights the ecological and cultural importance of elephants. India hosts nearly 60% of the world’s wild Asian elephant population and has strengthened conservation through Project Elephant, Elephant Reserves and protected corridors. Scientific monitoring, technology-driven conservation and community participation further support coexistence between people and elephants. These sustained efforts reflect the Government of India’s commitment to safeguarding elephants, ecosystems and India’s natural heritage.

The Gentle Giant of India's Forests

India is home to nearly 60% of the world’s wild Asian elephants, highlighting its vital role in global elephant conservation. Elephants hold deep cultural significance and play a vital role in healthy ecosystems. As a keystone species, they sustain forests, support biodiversity and maintain ecological balance. The Synchronous All India Population Estimation of Elephants (SAIEE) 2021–25 estimates India’s wild elephant population at 22,446. These elephants are protected across 33 Elephant Reserves and 150 identified corridors.

This rich elephant heritage also brings a responsibility to address growing conservation challenges. World Elephant Day, observed annually on 12 August, highlights the need for sustained global action. India’s conservation efforts address habitat loss, fragmentation, poaching, illegal wildlife trade and human-elephant conflict. The country combines legal protection, habitat conservation, scientific monitoring and community participation as part of its conservation efforts. Technology-driven measures further strengthen these efforts and support the long-term survival of elephants in the wild.

The Enduring Significance of Elephants in India

Elephants are integral to India’s natural and cultural heritage. Their significance spans ecosystem health, cultural traditions and community identities.

Ecological Importance

Elephants are foundational species that shape forest structure and ecosystem functioning. They are migratory in nature, with home ranges spanning 100–3,000 km². As they move long distances, they create pathways and water holes that benefit other wildlife. Their feeding habits support nutrient cycling, and bring about seed dispersal that aids forest regeneration. This helps in connecting fragmented forests and creating favourable conditions for thriving genetic diversity. Protecting elephants therefore strengthens ecological connectivity, forest health and wider biodiversity.

Cultural and Social Importance

Elephants have shaped India’s religious traditions, cultural practices and community identities for centuries. Lord Ganesha represents wisdom and the removal of obstacles in North Indian traditions. Elephants historically symbolised authority and prestige as royal emblems. Temple elephants remain part of religious rituals and festivals in South India. Communities across the Northeast worship Lord Ganesha as a manifestation of their deities and regard elephants with deep respect. Some communities traditionally view elephants as elders and symbols of wisdom. These traditions highlight the enduring place of elephants in India’s cultural heritage and community life.

Counting the Giants: Where India's Elephants Stand Today

India's elephant conservation story is best told through numbers. From reserve networks to corridor restoration, each figure reflects decades of sustained institutional effort.

Project Elephant: A Comprehensive Conservation Framework

Project Elephant is the Government of India's flagship initiative for elephant conservation. Implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), the programme provides financial and technical support to States for protecting elephant habitats, conserving captive elephants and mitigating human-elephant conflict. It also promotes science-driven conservation through AI-enabled monitoring, radio-collaring, genetic databases and early warning systems.

DNA-based Sampling Scientific monitoring under Project Elephant has strengthened elephant population assessment. SAIEE 2021–25 used India’s first DNA-based synchronised elephant census. Scientists analysed dung samples to identify individual elephants through unique genetic fingerprints. This helped detect repeat samples across landscapes and improve population estimates. SAIEE combined DNA profiling, block counts and line-transect surveys, strengthening the scientific rigour of elephant population assessment.

Securing India's Elephant Corridors

Elephant corridors play an important role in elephant conservation in India. They connect erstwhile natural habitats that have got fragmented due to human development or other reasons. The elephant corridors are habitats that have been developed to connect fragmented habitats. They are essential for maintaining healthy and genetically diverse elephant populations by enabling safe movement between fragmented habitats and helping reduce human-elephant conflict. They also support long-term population viability by maintaining ecological connectivity. Under Project Elephant, the Government has identified and validated elephant corridors across 14 elephant-range states.

According to Elephant Corridors of India, 2023, prepared with technical support from the Wildlife Institute of India, these corridors span across four regions. The East-Central region has 52 corridors, followed by the North-East (48), Southern (32) and Northern (18) regions. West Bengal has the highest number, with 26 corridors. This accounts for more than 17% of the national total. The network includes 19 inter-state corridors and six transboundary corridors connecting India and Nepal. Monitoring shows increased elephant use in 59 corridors (40%), stable use in 29 (19%), declining use in 29 (19%), and impaired conditions in 15 corridors.

Protecting these corridors strengthens habitat connectivity, reduces conflict and supports the long-term conservation of India’s elephant populations.

Sustained Corridor Conservation The Government continues to strengthen these ecological lifelines through scientific monitoring, boundary delineation and integration into State working and management plans. Currently, 150 corridors support elephant movement. These sustained efforts are strengthening habitat connectivity and securing safer movement for elephants across India's forest landscapes.

Growing the Reserve Network

Elephant Reserves have expanded steadily since 2014, now covering 80,777 km across 14 major elephant-range states. The expansion has brought an additional 8,610 km² under protection, securing critical habitats and strengthening ecological connectivity. It has also improved scientific management and created a stronger foundation for the long-term survival of India's wild elephant population.

Collectively, Project Elephant, scientific population estimation, protected reserves and connected corridors have transformed elephant conservation into an integrated landscape-level programme. These initiatives demonstrate the Government's commitment to combining traditional conservation values with modern science to secure the future of the Asian elephant.

Beyond the Count: Protecting Every Elephant

Estimating elephant populations is only one part of conservation. Long-term success depends on safer habitats, stronger legal safeguards and peaceful coexistence with communities. The Government of India has adopted a comprehensive conservation approach that combines science, technology, infrastructure and public welfare. These initiatives protect elephants both inside forests and across shared landscapes.

India has sought to improve how elephant landscapes are managed. The Management Effectiveness Evaluation framework for Elephant Reserves was launched in 2023 and tested in four representative reserves—Shivalik, Kaziranga–Karbi Anglong, Mayurbhanj and Nilgiri. Building on the pilot experience, the Government is taking this framework to Elephant Reserves across the country, supported through CAMPA funding. This institutionalises transparent assessment and adaptive management based on measurable conservation outcomes.

More recently, the Ministry has taken this landscape-based approach a step further by developing Regional Action Plans for all elephant-bearing regions of the country. These plans recognise that elephants range across State boundaries and that challenges relating to habitat connectivity, human-elephant conflict and landscape management require coordinated action across jurisdictions. The Regional Action Plans provide a common framework for States to undertake priority conservation and conflict-mitigation interventions at the landscape scale.

Making Railways Safer for Elephants

The Government has taken decisive steps to reduce elephant deaths along railway corridors. Joint surveys covered 127 sensitive railway stretches spanning 3,452.4 km. Further, Seventy-seven stretches across 14 States, covering 1,965.2 km, have been recommended for mitigation measures involving 705 structures, including underpasses, overpasses, ramps, level crossings and bridge modifications. These structural interventions are being complemented by technologies such as optical-fibre-based intrusion detection, seismic sensors and thermal cameras.

Also, AI-enabled Distributed Acoustic Sensing systems now provide real-time alerts to loco pilots, station masters and control rooms. Every train collision involving elephants is jointly investigated with the concerned State Forest Department. These sustained interventions reduced train-hit elephant deaths from 26 in 2013 to 12 in 2024, a decline of more than 50 percent.

Guarding Captive Elephants Through Genetics

The Government has strengthened safeguards against the illegal trade and movement of captive elephants through science-based monitoring. Under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, cases related to sale, transport and procurement are referred to State Chief Wildlife Wardens for action. The Gajah Suchana mobile application has created a national genetic database containing DNA profiles, morphological characteristics and ownership details of every registered captive elephant. The database verifies identity before movement and provides reliable forensic evidence during legal proceedings.

Captive Elephant (Transfer or Transport) Rules, 2024 To regulate the movement of captive elephants, the Government notified the Captive Elephant (Transfer or Transport) Rules, 2024. A High-Powered Committee examines interstate transfers of captive elephants. It was constituted under the Supreme Court's order dated March 3, 2023. Together, the application, the rules and the committee strengthen transparency and curb illegal transfer of captive elephants.

Supporting Communities for Peaceful Coexistence

Conservation succeeds when communities become equal partners in protecting wildlife. The Government provides ex-gratia assistance under the Centrally Sponsored Schemes Project Tiger and Elephant and Development of Wildlife Habitats. Assistance includes ₹10 lakh for death or permanent incapacitation, ₹2 lakh for grievous injury, treatment costs up to ₹25,000 for minor injuries, and compensation for crop and property losses as per State and UT norms.

The Government has further strengthened conflict management through the Human-Wildlife Conflict Advisory. It recommends hotspot mapping, rapid response teams, State and district-level review committees and faster compensation. Elephant-specific conflict mitigation guidelines, issued in 2023, further improve coordination among stakeholders. Together, these measures protect both elephants and people, strengthening safe and sustainable coexistence across India's elephant landscapes.

Reverence to Responsibility

India’s relationship with elephants reflects a unique harmony between civilisational values and modern conservation. Revered for centuries, elephants continue to inspire India’s commitment to protecting nature and maintaining ecological balance. This legacy is now strengthened through scientific research, technology, strong institutions and community participation.

The Government of India has developed a comprehensive framework for elephant conservation. Efforts include securing habitats, expanding Elephant Reserves, protecting corridors, improving railway safety and regulating captive elephant movement. Support for communities affected by human-elephant conflict further strengthens coexistence between people and wildlife.

As India observes World Elephant Day 2026, its commitment to elephant conservation remains steadfast. Every protected habitat, restored corridor and community partnership strengthens the future of the Asian elephant. Under Viksit Bharat, India continues to protect both its natural heritage and civilisational legacy for future generations.

Ministry of Heavy Industries

Ministry of Heavy Industries, under the SAMARTH centres has trained approximately 33000 persons

12 AUG 2026 11:26AM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Heavy Industries under the Scheme for Enhancement of Competitiveness in the Indian Capital Goods Sector has undertaken below mentioned initiatives for skill development:-

1. Setting up of four Smart Advanced Manufacturing and Rapid Transformation Hub (SAMARTH) Centres to promote Industry 4.0.

2. Setting up of Common Engineering Facility Centre (CEFC) at Welding Research Institute (WRI), Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL), Trichy for skilling in advanced welding technologies.

3. Development of 23 Qualification Packages by ASDC

4. Development of 23 Qualification Packages by CGSSC

5. Creation of 12 Qualification Packages by IASC SSC

Further as per information provided by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), MSDE has undertaken initiatives for strengthening the skilling ecosystem through its Schemes and initiatives. Flagship Schemes administered by MSDE include Pradhan MantriKaushalVikasYojana (PMKVY), Jan ShikshanSansthan (JSS), and the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) across all sectors including heavy industries and manufacturing sectors.

The Ministry of Heavy Industries, under the SAMARTH centres has trained approximately 33000 persons. Further under the CEFC at WRI, BHEL, Trichy more than approximately 8500 persons have been trained during the last three years.

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship under its Pradhan MantriKaushalVikasYojana (PMKVY) has trained candidates in various sectors. PMKVY 4.0 is the current version of the scheme under implementation since FY 2022-23. Under PMKVY 4.0, 27,31,699 candidates have been trained during the last three years.

Total enrolment in ITIs in courses under Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) in Capital Goods & Manufacturing sector during the last three years is 12,53,158.

(c) and (d): As per information provided by the MSDE, PMKVY 4.0 is a demand driven scheme wherein Training centres (TC) are accredited/ affiliated based on the proposals submitted by the Project Implement Agencies, after taking the skill gap into account. As on 30.6.2026, PMKVY 4.0 has imparted training through 16,946 TC including 6,993 educational Institutions such as schools, colleges ITI, University, Skill University, Polytechnic.

Prime Minister's Office

Text of PM's speech during release of former President Shri Ram Nath Kovind's autobiography

12 AUG 2026 11:19AM by PIB Delhi

हमारे पूर्व राष्ट्रपति श्रीमान रामनाथ कोविंद जी, लोकसभा के अध्यक्ष आदरणीय ओम बिरला जी, श्रीमती सविता कोविंद जी, सभाग्रह में सभी वरिष्ठ जन बैठे हैं, सबका उल्लेख नहीं कर पाऊंगा, लेकिन मेरे लिए बहुत आनंद है कि एक पारिवारिक कार्यक्रम लग रहा है।

आज हमें श्री रामनाथ कोविंद जी की आत्मकथा के विमोचन का अवसर मिला है। मुझे खुशी है कि मुझे भी इस कार्यक्रम का हिस्सा बनने का सौभाग्य मिला है। कोविंद जी से मेरा बहुत लंबा परिचय रहा है, उन्हें करीब से जानने का भी अवसर मिला और राष्ट्रपति के रूप में उनका मार्गदर्शन और इस सबके साथ-साथ उनका मेरे प्रति विशेष स्नेह, उनकी आत्मीयता, ये मेरी बहुत बड़ी पूंजी रही है। मैंने उनके जीवन को जितना समझा है, उनकी कार्यक्षमताओं को जितना जाना है, मैं पूरे विश्वास से कह सकता हूं कि श्री रामनाथ कोविंद जी की ऑटो-बायोग्राफ़ी अपने आप में भारतीय लोकतंत्र और भारतीय समाज के लिए एक धरोहर बनेगी। कोविंद जी की जीवन यात्रा, समाज और राष्ट्र के लिए उनका योगदान, ऐसा कितना कुछ है जिसके बारे में मैं विस्तार से बात कर सकता हूं, लेकिन बुक रिलीज़ में केवल ‘कर्टन रेज़र’ ही होना चाहिए। आप सब किताब का पूरा लाभ पढ़कर ही लें, तो ही ज्यादा अच्छा है।

कोविंद जी की जीवन यात्रा को आप उनके शब्दों में जानें, उनकी लेखनी को, उनके अनुभवों को देश की नई पीढ़ी पढ़े, इससे हर किसी को काफी कुछ सीखने को मिलेगा। मैं रामनाथ कोविंद जी को इस आत्मकथा के लिए बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूं।

कोविंद जी ने अपनी इस पुस्तक को बहुत ही सटीक नाम दिया है- “Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles” कहने का भाव ये कि जीवन और जीवन के संघर्ष उनके व्यक्तिगत हैं, लेकिन उन संघर्षों के परिणामस्वरूप मिली जीत, भारत के गणतंत्र की है, भारत के लोकतंत्र की है।

हम सब अक्सर अनुभव करते हैं कि इंसान का एक स्वभाव होता है, लोग अपनी सफलता का श्रेय खुद को देते हैं और जीवन की मुश्किलों के लिए, कठिनाइयों के लिए समाज को जिम्मेदार ठहराते हैं। लेकिन, जब हृदय उदार हो, भारतीय संस्कार हों, तब व्यक्ति समाज की कमियाँ निकालने में समय नहीं गँवाता, वो उसके सकारात्मक पक्ष पर फोकस करता है, वो अपनी सफलता में समाज को बराबर का भागीदार मानता है। कोविंद जी की आत्मकथा और उसका शीर्षक इसके उदाहरण हैं। आप उनका जीवन देखिए, एक बेहद सामान्य परिवार में, कानपुर देहात में उनका जन्म हुआ। कोविंद जी ने अभी भी कुछ वर्णन किया और अपनी किताब में भी लिखा है, कैसे गर्मी के मौसम में एक दिन उनके घर में आग लग गई, उनकी माँ अपनी चिंता छोड़कर घर की चीजों को बचा रही थीं। आखिर, एक सामान्य परिवार में, माँ के लिए एक-एक चीज बच्चों के पालन-पोषण का जरिया होती है। उसी कोशिश में, आग में फंसकर उनकी माता जी की मृत्यु हो गई। आप कल्पना कर सकते हैं, छोटी सी उम्र में इस तरह की घटना, माँ को इस तरह खो देना, ये कितना दर्दनाक रहा होगा। मैं तो भाग्यशाली रहा हूं, मेरी मां 100 साल से भी अधिक जीवित रही और मुझे आशीर्वाद देती रही। उसके बावजूद भी, आज भी मैं मां की कमी महसूस करता हूं।

उनके जीवन का एक ऐसा दर्दनाक ये घटनाक्रम था, कोई भी इससे टूट सकता था, लेकिन कोविंद जी को उन मुश्किलों ने मजबूत किया। पड़ोस की एक माता जी ने उनके पालन-पोषण में मदद की। इससे उन्होंने समाज की एकता और सौहार्द की ताकत को समझा। इस घटना के बाद कोविंद जी के जीवन में उनके पिता की भूमिका और बड़ी हो गई और जिस तरह से उन्होंने अपने परिवार को संभाला, बच्चों को संस्कार दिये, इसीलिए, कोविंद जी अपने पिता को अपना हीरो मानते हैं।

बचपन के इन संघर्षों के बीच, कोविंद जी ने शिक्षा को, अपने सामर्थ्य को बढ़ाने का मार्ग बनाया। उन्होंने मेहनत की, उन्होंने संसाधनों की कमी को कमजोरी नहीं बनने दिया। और, एक ऐसे मुकाम तक पहुंचे, जिसकी कल्पना भी तब लोगों ने नहीं की थी। वो भारत जैसे विशाल देश के राष्ट्रपति बने।

इतने बड़े पद पर पहुंचने के बाद भी कोविंद जी का विनम्र व्यक्तित्व, उनकी सादगी ऐसे ही कायम रही। मुझे याद है प्रधानमंत्री के तौर पर मैं राष्ट्रपति भवन में उनसे मिलने जाता था। प्रोटोकॉल के हिसाब से जो बातें नहीं हो सकती हैं, वो बातें वो करते थे। वो प्रधानमंत्री को छोड़ने के लिए गाड़ी के दरवाजे तक आते थे। मैं शुरू में उनको प्रार्थना करता रहता था, प्लीज आप ऐसा मत कीजिए, लेकिन उन्होंने जीवन के आखिर तक अपनी उस विनम्रता को कभी छोड़ा नहीं। राष्ट्रपति बनने के बाद जब वे अपने गांव परौंख गए, तो उन्होंने वहाँ अपने गुरुओं के पैर छूकर उन्हें प्रणाम किया। गाँव की मिट्टी को नमन करके उन्होंने गाँव के सामान्य लोगों का धन्यवाद किया। पूरे देश ने वो भावुक दृश्य देखा था। उनके इस आचरण ने दुनिया के सामने भारत के संस्कारों की ऐसी तस्वीर सामने रखी, जिस पर हर भारतवासी गर्व करता है।

गुलामी के सैकड़ों साल में हमारे देश ने आर्थिक और सामाजिक रूप से बहुत कुछ खोया था। हमारे पूर्वजों ने सदियों तक संघर्ष किया। महात्मा गांधी, बाबा साहब अंबेडकर, ज्योतिबा फुले, सावित्रबाई फुले, ऐसी कितनी ही महान विभूतियों ने भारत के नवनिर्माण का सपना देखा था। एक ऐसा भारत जहां गरीब से गरीब, वंचित से वंचित को शिखर तक पहुँचने का अवसर मिल सके। कोविंद जी जैसे व्यक्तित्वों ने अपने श्रम और काबिलियत से केवल खुद का जीवन ही बदला, इतना नहीं है, उन्होंने सदियों के उस स्वप्न को, उस विज़न को भी साकार करने में अपनी अहम भूमिका निभाई है। और इस दिशा में हम सबके प्रयास अभी भी जारी हैं। हमें भविष्य में कोविंद जी जैसे अनेकों युवा चाहिए, जो परेशानियों से परास्त न हों, जो मुश्किलों के सामने मायूस न हों, बल्कि अपनी मेहनत से हर मंजिल को आसान बनाने का हौसला रखें। इसी बदलाव से सशक्त भारत के निर्माण का संकल्प पूरा होगा। यहीं से आत्मनिर्भर और विकसित भारत का रास्ता बनेगा।

ऐसे युवाशक्ति के निर्माण के लिए जो प्रेरणा चाहिए, कोविंद जी की ऑटोबायोग्राफ़ी उसका अहम स्रोत बन सकती है।

कोविंद जी ने अपनी जीवनी में मोरारजी भाई देसाई के साथ अनुभवों के बारे में भी इसमें विस्तार से बताया है। कोविंद जी के भीतर देशसेवा की जो भावना थी, मोरारजी भाई के साथ काम करके उन्हें जो सीखने को मिला, जो रास्ता मिला। कोविंद जी ने राजनीति और समाजसेवा को अपना मार्ग बनाया। वो अपने कर्तव्यों के लिए समर्पित रहे। सेवा को उन्होंने अपना लक्ष्य बनाकर काम किया। संसद में उनका कार्यकाल गवाह है। राज्यपाल के रूप में भी उन्होंने एक उदाहरण प्रस्तुत किया। राष्ट्रपति के रूप में भी हमें उनकी यही कर्तव्यनिष्ठा दिखाई देती रही। यहाँ तक कि राष्ट्रपति जैसे सर्वोच्च पद से सेवामुक्त होने के बाद भी उन्होंने विश्राम नहीं लिया है। वो अभी भी ‘एक देश, एक चुनाव’ One Nation, One Election जैसे महत्वपूर्ण विषय पर काम कर रहे हैं। देश को जगा रहे हैं। ये एक ऐसा विषय है, जिसका समाधान देश के लोकतंत्र का नया अध्याय शुरू कर सकता है। मैं मानता हूँ, कोविंद जी की इस कर्तव्यनिष्ठा और सेवाभाव से देश के लोग बहुत कुछ सीख सकते हैं।

सामाजिक जीवन में सक्रिय रहते हुये ऑटोबायोग्राफ़ी के लिए समय निकाल पाना बहुत मुश्किल होता है। कोविंद जी ने ये काम हम सबके लिए किया है, क्योंकि उनके जीवन में ऐसा कितना कुछ है, जिसमें गरीब वंचित तबके से आए तमाम लोग अपने जीवन की परछाई देख सकते हैं। कैसे एक साधारण परिवार मुश्किल हालातों में भी जीवन की शुचिता और ईमानदारी से समझौता नहीं करता, कैसे वही आदर्श आगे चलकर हमारे जीवन का आधार बनते हैं, हमारे कठिन समय के मूल्य किस तरह जीवनभर हमें रोशनी देते हैं, कैसे इस पवित्रता से हमें राष्ट्र सेवा की शक्ति मिलती है। अलग-अलग पदों का दायित्व निभाते हुए, कोविंद जी ने समाज को निरंतर इसकी प्रेरणा दी है।

मुझे विश्वास है, कोविंद जी की ऑटोबायोग्राफ़ी, इसमें उनके जीवन की ही नहीं, बल्कि हमारे लोकतंत्र की भी अहम स्मृतियाँ सुरक्षित होंगी। मैं एक बार फिर उन्हें उनकी आत्मकथा के लिए शुभकामनाएं देता हूं। और मैं खास करके युवा पीढ़ी से आग्रह करूंगा, रील का जमाना है, सोशल मीडिया में इनफ्लुएंसर आपको खींच के कहीं-कहीं ले जाते हैं। इस शॉर्टकट के युग में भी एक बात हम जरूर याद रखें, रेलवे स्टेशन पर लिखा हुआ होता है, कुछ लोगों को पटरी पर कूद कर के जाने की आदत होती है, ब्रिज पर नहीं जाते। तो वहां लिखा होता है, शॉर्टकट विल कट यू शॉर्ट। और अगर शॉर्टकट के रास्ते से भी कहीं बाहर निकलना है, तो मैं नौजवानों को कहूंगा आपको जिसका भी पसंद हो ऑटोबायोग्राफी जरूर पढ़ें। ऑटोबायोग्राफी उस कालखंड की इतिहास की घटनाओं को अलग तरीके से समझने का अवसर देती है। इतिहास से काफी निकट होता है वो कालखंड बायोग्राफी का और इसलिए मैं जरूर चाहूंगा कि कोविंद जी की जो मेहनत है, वो आने वाली पीढ़ियों को काम आए, युवा पीढ़ी को विशेष रूप से काम आए। बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएं। बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

India Reaffirms Commitment to Elephant Conservation on World Elephant Day 2026

Securing the Future of Elephants Means Securing Our Forests, Biodiversity and Ecological Heritage: Shri Bhupender Yadav

12 AUG 2026 11:19AM by PIB Delhi

On the occasion of World Elephant Day 2026, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, reaffirmed India’s commitment to securing a shared future for elephants and people.

In a post on social media, the Minister noted that India has 33 Elephant Reserves across 14 States and 150 scientifically validated elephant corridors. Shri Yadav said advanced population monitoring and stronger measures would mitigate human-elephant conflict are strengthening elephant conservation.

On #WorldElephantDay, we reaffirm India’s commitment to securing a shared future for elephants and people.

With 33 Elephant Reserves across 14 States, 150 scientifically validated elephant corridors, advanced population monitoring and stronger measures to mitigate human-elephant… pic.twitter.com/jIdd1PXHMH

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) August 12, 2026

The Minister further stated, “when we secure the future of elephants, we secure our forests, biodiversity and ecological heritage”. The Minister called for an action to ensure that the elephant continues to walk freely through India’s forests and landscapes for generations to come.

On the occasion, in a social media post, Union MoS (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, stated that India is home to one of the richest and most diverse landscapes on Earth. Shri Singh said that nearly 60 per cent of the world’s wild Asian elephants live in India, making them a living symbol of the country’s ecological heritage. The Minister further stated that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India’s elephant reserves stand as a testament to the country’s commitment towards conservation.

India is home to one of the richest and most diverse landscapes on Earth. On #WorldElephantDay we can proudly say that nearly 60% of the world’s wild Asian elephants live here, a living symbol of our ecological heritage. They embody majestic beauty, hold deep religious and… pic.twitter.com/Wns3CR9YlE

— Kirti Vardhan Singh (@KVSinghMPGonda) August 12, 2026

Shri Kriti Vardhan Singh also highlighted the role of elephants as ecosystem engineers. Shri Singh said that as elephants roam, they disperse seeds across long distances, giving rise to new plants, and that every step of an elephant helps keep nature in balance. He called upon everyone to unite to protect and preserve these gentle giants.
